questions.q: Which role is Power BI's own service account configured to connect as?
options: DRIFTWOOD_ANALYST
DRIFTWOOD_TRANSFORMER
DRIFTWOOD_COMPLIANCE
ACCOUNTADMIN
questions.explain: DRIFTWOOD_ANALYST is the read-only, marts-only role -- and the one whose queries see the email column masked.

questions.q: Which two roles see dim_subscribers.email unmasked, and why?
options: DRIFTWOOD_COMPLIANCE (a real, specific business need) and DRIFTWOOD_TRANSFORMER (the pipeline's service account, which needs it to build the pipeline)
DRIFTWOOD_ANALYST and DRIFTWOOD_COMPLIANCE
Every role sees the email unmasked by default
No role ever sees the unmasked email, including DRIFTWOOD_COMPLIANCE
questions.explain: Each unmasked role has a specific, named functional reason -- not broad access granted out of convenience.

questions.q: Why does this lesson prefer masking over simply not granting DRIFTWOOD_ANALYST any privilege on the email column at all?
options: Masking lets a broad SELECT * query keep working with the value hidden, instead of erroring out entirely for any query referencing that column
Snowflake does not allow revoking access to individual columns
Masking is faster to execute than an access restriction
There is no real difference between the two approaches
questions.explain: A column-level access restriction breaks any query that references it (including SELECT *); masking lets the query succeed with the sensitive value safely hidden instead.

questions.q: What does the masking policy's CASE logic check to decide whether to return the real value?
options: CURRENT_ROLE(), checking whether it's DRIFTWOOD_COMPLIANCE or DRIFTWOOD_TRANSFORMER
The current time of day
Whether the query includes a WHERE clause
The subscriber's own cancellation status
questions.explain: The masking policy evaluates CURRENT_ROLE() at query time -- the same CASE/CURRENT_ROLE() pattern taught in the Snowflake course's own masking lesson.

questions.q: Does the stored email value in dim_subscribers ever actually change because of this masking policy?
options: No -- the stored value is untouched; Snowflake substitutes a masked version only as query results are returned
Yes -- the masking policy permanently overwrites the stored value for unauthorized roles
Yes -- but only for rows belonging to cancelled subscribers
The stored value is deleted entirely once a masking policy is attached
questions.explain: Masking is applied at query time only -- the underlying stored data is never altered, which is exactly why the same policy can show different results to different roles on the same query.
